items.title: Unitary conjugation, generator transport and strong commutation of self-adjoint observables
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of
Dependent Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral and
Bochner suppliers. Fix $\hbar>0$, let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space
([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $K$ and $A$ be self-adjoint operators on $H$ with
spectral projection-valued measures $E_K$ and $E_A$
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]), let $W\in\mathcal B(H)$ be unitary
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]],
[[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]), and put
$$U_K(t):=e^{-itK/\hbar},\qquad U_A(s):=e^{-isA/\hbar}\qquad(s,t\in\mathbb R)$$
in the spectral calculus of [[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]], which are
strongly continuous one-parameter unitary groups
([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]],
[[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]). Write
$\Phi_K(g)=\int g\,dE_K$ for bounded Borel $g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$
([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]), and let
$K_W:=WKW^{*}$ with $D(K_W):=WD(K)$. Then:

(a) $K_W$ is self-adjoint with spectral projection-valued measure
$$E_{K_W}(B)=WE_K(B)W^{*}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
its flow satisfies $e^{-itK_W/\hbar}=WU_K(t)W^{*}$ for every $t$, and the
conjugated family $s\mapsto WU_A(s)W^{*}$ is a strongly continuous
one-parameter unitary group whose infinitesimal generator is
$-\frac{i}{\hbar}WAW^{*}$ with domain $WD(A)$
([[def-infinitesimal-generator-of-a-unitary-group]]);

(b) the following are equivalent:

  (i) $U_A(s)U_K(t)=U_K(t)U_A(s)$ for all $s,t\in\mathbb R$;

  (ii) $E_A(B)E_K(C)=E_K(C)E_A(B)$ for all Borel sets $B,C\subseteq\mathbb R$;

  (iii) $U_K(t)D(A)=D(A)$ and $U_K(t)AU_K(t)^{*}=A$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$;

(c) if a bounded $B\in\mathcal B(H)$ satisfies $BU_K(t)=U_K(t)B$ for every
$t\in\mathbb R$, then $B\Phi_K(g)=\Phi_K(g)B$ for every bounded Borel
$g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$; in particular $BE_K(C)=E_K(C)B$ for every Borel
$C\subseteq\mathbb R$;

(d) if (i)-(iii) of (b) hold, then $E_A(B)U_K(t)=U_K(t)E_A(B)$ for every Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$.

items.title: The spatial rotation action on the component-valued wave-function space
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the cited spectral suppliers. Fix an integer $r\ge1$ and $\hbar>0$, let
$H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ with inner product linear in the
first argument ([[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-hilbert-space]]), let $Q_{j},P_{k}$ be the componentwise position and
momentum operators ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]
clause (a)), and let $\mathcal S^{(r)}=\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$
and $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the componentwise Schwartz and
Sobolev classes ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]],
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]). Let $SO(3)$ be the special orthogonal
group with its Euclidean topology ([[def-cm-special-orthogonal-group]],
[[lem-cm-so3-is-a-matrix-group]]) and for $R\in SO(3)$ define, componentwise,
$$\bigl(U(R)f\bigr)_{l}(x):=f_{l}(R^{-1}x)\qquad(x\in\mathbb R^{3},\ l=1,\dots,r).$$
Let $U^{(r)}$ be the unitary momentum representation of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] and $M_R$ the bounded operator
on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dp;\mathbb C^{r})$ given by $(M_Rg)(p):=g(R^{-1}p)$. Then:

(a) $U(R)$ is a well-defined unitary operator for every $R$, with
$U(I)=\mathrm{id}$, $U(RS)=U(R)U(S)$ and $U(R)^{-1}=U(R^{-1})$ for all
$R,S\in SO(3)$; and for every $f\in H^{(r)}$ the orbit map
$R\mapsto U(R)f$ is continuous on $SO(3)$ ([[def-metric-continuity]]).
Moreover $U(R)\mathcal S^{(r)}=\mathcal S^{(r)}$ and
$U(R)W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})=W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$
for $m=1,2$;

(b) $U^{(r)}U(R)U^{(r)-1}=M_R$. For $a\in\mathbb R^3$ define the maximal directional operators
$$Q(a):=M_{a\cdot x},\qquad P(a):=U^{(r)-1}M_{a\cdot p}U^{(r)},$$
where each multiplier has its maximal domain, namely the classes for which its product is in $L^2$. Thus
$$D(Q(a))=\{f:(a\cdot x)f\in L^2\},\qquad D(P(a))=\{f:(a\cdot p)U^{(r)}f\in L^2\}.$$
They are self-adjoint (for $a=0$ they are the zero operator on all of $H^{(r)}$). On the common coordinate domains they agree with $\sum_l a_lQ_l$ and $\sum_l a_lP_l$, respectively. The full conjugation identities, including domains, are
$$U(R)Q_jU(R)^{-1}=Q(Re_j),\qquad U(R)P_kU(R)^{-1}=P(Re_k),$$
$$U(R)D(Q_j)=D(Q(Re_j)),\qquad U(R)D(P_k)=D(P(Re_k)).$$
In particular, an individual coordinate domain is preserved when $Re_j=\pm e_j$ (respectively $Re_k=\pm e_k$); no such preservation is asserted for an arbitrary rotation. The expressions $\sum_lR_{lj}Q_l$ and $\sum_lR_{lk}P_l$ in full operator identities mean these maximal directional realizations.

(c) with the free operator $H_{0}:=\frac{1}{2m_{0}}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2}$ for a
parameter $m_{0}>0$, whose domain is $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$,
one has $U(R)H_{0}U(R)^{-1}=H_{0}$; and for a real bounded measurable
$V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ with multiplier $M_{V}$ (multiplication by $V$)
and $V_{R}(x):=V(R^{-1}x)$ one has $U(R)M_{V}U(R)^{-1}=M_{V_{R}}$, so that
$U(R)H_{V}U(R)^{-1}=H_{V_{R}}$ for the free-plus-$V$ operator $H_{V}$ with
domain $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$.

items.title: The spatial parity action on the component-valued wave-function space
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix an integer $r\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$, let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ with inner product
linear in the first argument ([[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]], [[def-hilbert-space]]), let
$Q_{j},P_{k}$ be the componentwise position and momentum operators
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a)), and
let $\mathcal S^{(r)}=\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ and
$W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the componentwise Schwartz and
Sobolev classes ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]],
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]). Define the **parity action**
$$\bigl(\Pi f\bigr)_{l}(x):=f_{l}(-x)\qquad(x\in\mathbb R^{3},\ l=1,\dots,r),$$
let $U^{(r)}$ be the unitary momentum representation of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]], and let $M_{-1}$ be the
reflection operator on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dp;\mathbb C^{r})$ defined by
$(M_{-1}g)(p):=g(-p)$. This composition operator is not pointwise
multiplication by a function; reflection substitution makes it unitary. Then:

(a) $\Pi$ is a well-defined unitary operator with $\Pi^{2}=\mathrm{id}$ and
$\Pi^{*}=\Pi$; moreover $\Pi\mathcal S^{(r)}=\mathcal S^{(r)}$ and
$\Pi W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})=W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$
for $m=1,2$;

(b) $\Pi D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j})$ and $\Pi Q_{j}\Pi=-Q_{j}$; $\Pi D(P_{k})=D(P_{k})$
and $\Pi P_{k}\Pi=-P_{k}$;

(c) $U^{(r)}\Pi U^{(r)-1}=M_{-1}$;

(d) with $H_{0}=\frac{1}{2m_{0}}\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}$ for a parameter
$m_{0}>0$ and a real bounded measurable $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$, writing
$V_{P}(x):=V(-x)$ and $H_{V}=H_{0}+M_{V}$, one has $\Pi H_{0}\Pi=H_{0}$ and
$\Pi M_{V}\Pi=M_{V_{P}}$, so $\Pi H_{V}\Pi=H_{V_{P}}$.

items.title: Coordinate-rotation generators on the Schwartz classes and their commutators
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix an integer $r\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$, let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ with the
componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ and the Schwartz class
$\mathcal S^{(r)}=\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]],
[[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]), and let $U(R)$ for $R\in SO(3)$ be
the spatial rotation action of [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]]
(so that $(U(R)f)(x)=f(R^{-1}x)$ componentwise and $U$ is a strongly continuous
unitary representation). For $i=1,2,3$ define the rotation matrices
$$R_{1}(t):=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&\cos t&-\sin t\\0&\sin t&\cos t\end{pmatrix},\quad R_{2}(t):=\begin{pmatrix}\cos t&0&\sin t\\0&1&0\\-\sin t&0&\cos t\end{pmatrix},\quad R_{3}(t):=\begin{pmatrix}\cos t&-\sin t&0\\\sin t&\cos t&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix},$$
put $U_{i}(t):=U(R_{i}(t))$, and let $L_{i}$ be the self-adjoint operator with
$U_{i}(t)=e^{-itL_{i}/\hbar}$ furnished by Stone's theorem
([[thm-stone-one-parameter-unitary-groups]],
[[def-infinitesimal-generator-of-a-unitary-group]]). Then:

(a) for each $i$ the family $t\mapsto U_{i}(t)$ is a strongly continuous
one-parameter unitary group with $U_{i}(s+t)=U_{i}(s)U_{i}(t)$ and
$U_{i}(0)=\mathrm{id}$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]);

(b) for every $\psi\in\mathcal S^{(r)}$ the curve $t\mapsto U_{i}(t)\psi$ is
differentiable at $t=0$ into $H^{(r)}$ with
$$\frac{d}{dt}\Big|_{t=0}U_{i}(t)\psi=-\sum_{j=1}^{3}(e_{i}\times x)_{j}\,D_{j}\psi,$$
and consequently $\mathcal S^{(r)}\subseteq D(L_{i})$ and
$$L_{i}\psi=-i\hbar\sum_{j=1}^{3}(e_{i}\times x)_{j}D_{j}\psi=\sum_{j,k=1}^{3}\varepsilon_{ijk}\,Q_{j}P_{k}\psi\qquad(\psi\in\mathcal S^{(r)});$$

(c) $L_{i}\mathcal S^{(r)}\subseteq\mathcal S^{(r)}$ for each $i$, and on
$\mathcal S^{(r)}$ the commutation relations hold:
$$L_{i}L_{k}\psi-L_{k}L_{i}\psi=i\hbar\sum_{j=1}^{3}\varepsilon_{ikj}\,L_{j}\psi\qquad(\psi\in\mathcal S^{(r)}).$$
(d) For each $i$ the Schwartz class is a core for $L_i$: on $D(L_i)$
the graph norm
$$\|\psi\|_{L_i}:=\bigl(\|\psi\|_{H^{(r)}}^{2}+\hbar^{-2}\|L_i\psi\|_{H^{(r)}}^{2}\bigr)^{1/2}$$
makes $\mathcal S^{(r)}$ dense in $D(L_i)$ (equivalently, the graph closure of
$L_i|_{\mathcal S^{(r)}}$ is $L_i$). This norm is equivalent to the ordinary
graph norm because $\hbar>0$ is fixed.

items.title: The free flow as a unimodular multiplier in the momentum representation
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the choice hypotheses of
the cited spectral suppliers. Fix an integer $r\ge1$, a mass parameter $m>0$ and
$\hbar>0$, let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ with the
componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]], let $U^{(r)}$ be
the momentum unitary of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]], and
let
$$H_{0}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2},\qquad D(H_{0})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),$$
which is self-adjoint with the displayed domain
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (c) applied componentwise,
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a)). Write
$M_{a}$ for multiplication by a measurable function $a$ on
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dp;\mathbb C^{r})$ and put $f_{t}(p):=e^{-it|p|^{2}/(2m\hbar)}$
([[def-complex-exponential]]). Then:

(a) $U^{(r)}H_{0}U^{(r)-1}=M_{|p|^{2}/(2m)}$ as self-adjoint operators, with
domain $D(M_{|p|^{2}/(2m)})=\{g\in L^{2}:\ |p|^{2}g\in L^{2}\}$;

(b) $U^{(r)}\,e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\,U^{(r)-1}=M_{f_{t}}$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$;

(c) for every $\psi\in H^{(r)}$, every $t$ and almost every $p$,
$$\bigl(U^{(r)}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\psi\bigr)(p)=f_{t}(p)\,\bigl(U^{(r)}\psi\bigr)(p),\qquad \bigl|\bigl(U^{(r)}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\psi\bigr)(p)\bigr|=\bigl|\bigl(U^{(r)}\psi\bigr)(p)\bigr|;$$
consequently the spectral outcome law of each $P_{k}$ is independent of $t$;
and $e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\mathcal S^{(r)}=\mathcal S^{(r)}$ for every $t$, where
$\mathcal S^{(r)}=\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$.

items.title: Symmetries of the declared dynamics, unitary symmetry groups and conserved sharp observables
items.statement:
**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the
autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] for a **declared isolated
system** with state space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]])
and assigned energy observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ with spectral
projection-valued measure $E_H$ and flow
$U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]). Units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].

**(b) Symmetry of the dynamics.** A **symmetry of the declared dynamics**, or
simply a **symmetry**, is a unitary operator $S\in\mathcal B(H)$ with
$$S\,D(H_{\mathrm{op}})=D(H_{\mathrm{op}}),\qquad S\,H_{\mathrm{op}}=H_{\mathrm{op}}\,S\ \text{ on }D(H_{\mathrm{op}}).$$
The reading is the model's: a symmetry is a unitary that preserves the assigned
energy domain and commutes with the assigned energy operator on that domain;
the equivalent formulation by commutation with the flow $U(t)$, and the
concomitant conservation statements, are proved results of this page and are
not part of this definition. Neither the energy operator nor its potential or
coupling terms are assumed to possess any symmetry here.

**(c) Unitary symmetry group.** A **unitary symmetry group** of the declared
system is a group $G$ together with a map $g\mapsto S_g$ from $G$ into the
unitary operators of $H$ such that $S_e=I$, $S_{gh}=S_gS_h$ and every $S_g$ is
a symmetry in the sense of (b). When $G$ carries a topology, the group is
**strongly continuous** when $g\mapsto S_g f$ is continuous for every
$f\in H$; for the one-parameter case the concrete condition is that of
[[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]. The model's standard
candidate spatial symmetry groups and additional unitary symmetry actions,
which must satisfy clause (b) before any one of them is called a symmetry,
include:

1. the **spatial translations** $T_a$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (c),
   forming the group $\mathbb R^{3}$, with generator data supplied by
   [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (d);
2. the **spatial rotations** $U(R)$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]], forming the group $SO(3)$
   with its Euclidean topology, and their coordinate one-parameter subgroups,
   whose generators are the operators $L_{i}$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]];
3. the **spatial parity** action $\Pi$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-parity-action]], forming the two-element group
   $\{I,\Pi\}$;
4. in the **spinless scalar case** $H=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the
   **gauge phase multipliers** $G_{\chi}(t)$. No action on an internal factor
   is defined here. Given an open interval $I$, a real Borel
   function $\chi:\mathbb R^{3}\times I\to\mathbb R$ with unit
   $\mathrm{J\,s\,C^{-1}}$, a charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ with unit C,
   and $\hbar>0$ with unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$, define
   $$\bigl(G_{\chi}(t)\psi\bigr)(x):=\exp\!\bigl(iq\chi(x,t)/\hbar\bigr)\psi(x)\quad\text{for almost every }x,\qquad \psi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C).$$
   For each fixed $t$, this is a unitary operator. The real coefficients in
   the defining power series give
   $\overline{\exp(i\theta)}=\exp(-i\theta)$ for real $\theta$; by absolute
   convergence, the Cauchy product for $\exp(i\theta)\exp(-i\theta)$ groups
   the coefficient of degree $k$ as
   $\frac1{k!}\sum_{j=0}^{k}\binom{k}{j}(-1)^{k-j}$; the finite sum is
   $(1-1)^k$, hence is $1$ for $k=0$ and $0$ for $k\ge1$. Therefore
   $|\exp(i\theta)|=1$ and the inverse multiplier is
   $\exp\!\bigl(-iq\chi(\cdot,t)/\hbar\bigr)$. This definition asserts only its action on
   $L^{2}$; it assumes no regularity of $\chi$ and does not imply preservation
   of an unbounded energy domain. The gauge-covariance result treats only the
   additional regularity class stated by the prescribed-coupling postulate.

**(d) One-parameter symmetry group and generator.** A **one-parameter symmetry
group** is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$t\mapsto S_t=e^{-itA/\hbar}$ with every $S_t$ a symmetry in the sense of (b),
where $A$ is the self-adjoint **generator** furnished by Stone's theorem
([[thm-stone-one-parameter-unitary-groups]]); its declared unit is that of the
spectral coordinate of $A$. When $S_t=U(R_i(t))$ for a coordinate rotation
subgroup, $A$ is the operator $L_i$ above; when
$S_t=T_{te_j}$, $A$ is the momentum component $P_j$ in the reading of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (d).

**(e) Conserved sharp observables.** Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp
observable of the framework ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]).
It is **conserved along the flow** when its outcome law is independent of time
in every preparation: for every preparation $\rho$
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]) and every Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho(0)}(B),\qquad \rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}.$$
The conserved object is thus the outcome law of the assigned observable — a
probability measure on the Borel sets — and, where the moments exist, its
moments; the definition does not say that a single numerical value is revealed
at each time, and it identifies no laboratory quantity with the pair $(A,u_A)$.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the vocabulary of this page within
P1, P2 and P4 and the cited readings. They assert no symmetry of any concrete
model: whether $T_a$, $U(R)$ or $\Pi$ is a symmetry of a given bounded-potential
dynamics is decided by the conditional results of this page. The gauge
definition asserts only an $L^{2}$ unitary; a symmetry claim must separately
verify the energy-domain and commutation conditions of clause (b). Antiunitary
symmetries, superselection sectors, symmetries of preparations as opposed to
dynamics, and any empirical claim about which symmetries a laboratory system
possesses are outside this definition. The
parameter $a$ of a translation has the unit of length $u_H$ of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the rotation group and parity
act on the spatial factor only, in the readings of
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]] and
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-parity-action]], and the prescribed-coupling reading is
that of [[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-magnetic-schrodinger-operator]].
items.physical_scope: The symmetry and conservation vocabulary of the declared framework model: symmetries of the dynamics of a declared isolated system as unitaries preserving the energy domain and commuting with the energy operator, unitary symmetry groups and their strong continuity, one-parameter symmetry groups and their Stone generators, and the reading of a conserved sharp observable as one whose outcome law is time-independent in every preparation. The item fixes terminology and candidate actions of the model (translations, spatial rotations, parity, and explicitly defined gauge phase multipliers on the spinless scalar space); it asserts no symmetry of any concrete model potential or external coupling, no antiunitary or superselection structure, no apparatus realization and no empirical result.

items.title: Prescribed external electromagnetic coupling P5a: the minimal-coupling model and its gauge transformations
items.statement:
Adopt as a physical assumption of the framework, additional to P1-P5 and valid
only for the model of this page, the following prescribed-coupling statement
for a **spinless** particle. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom
of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice
hypotheses of the cited magnetic-operator suppliers.

**(i) Frame and particle data.** Fix a named Newtonian inertial frame in the
class adopted by
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]] (P5)
and a declared spinless particle of mass parameter $m>0$ and charge
parameter $q\in\mathbb R$; the model state space is the scalar component of the
massive model, $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, with the position and momentum
operators of the massive model. The frame, the mass and the charge are part of
the model specification; the frame is not derived from the potentials, and
$m$ and $q$ are empirical parameters of a species when one is identified.

**(ii) Admissible prescribed potentials.** The external data are an
**admissible pair** $(\mathbf A_{\rm ext},\Phi_{\rm ext})$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-magnetic-schrodinger-operator]]: real
classes $\mathbf A_{\rm ext}=(A_{1},A_{2},A_{3})$ with
$A_{j}\in L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb R)$ whose weak first derivatives
$D_{k}A_{j}$ are bounded, and $\Phi_{\rm ext}\in L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb R)$
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]],
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]). The potentials are **prescribed**: no
field equation, source model or back-reaction is assumed.

**(iii) Energy operator.** The model's energy operator is the
minimal-coupling magnetic Schrodinger operator
$$H_{\rm ext}:=K_{\mathbf A_{\rm ext},\Phi_{\rm ext}},\qquad D(H_{\rm ext})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C),$$
of [[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-magnetic-schrodinger-operator]], that is
$$H_{\rm ext}=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{j=1}^{3}\bigl(P_{j}-qA_{{\rm ext},j}(Q)\bigr)^{2}+q\,\Phi_{\rm ext}(Q)$$
on the displayed domain. This operator is self-adjoint with domain
$W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ by
[[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-bounded-coefficient-magnetic-operator]], so
it satisfies the self-adjointness requirement of the dynamics postulate P4 in
the reading of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]; the
adoption here is the identification of this operator as the energy of the
declared particle, which is a model assumption and not a consequence of
P1-P5.

**(iv) Units.** Use the units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]];
the additional assignments are: $\mathbf A_{\rm ext}$ in
$\mathrm{T\,m}=\mathrm{V\,s\,m^{-1}}$, $\Phi_{\rm ext}$ in V, $q$ in C, so
$q\mathbf A_{\rm ext}$ has momentum units and $q\Phi_{\rm ext}$ energy units.
The exponential of clause (vi) uses [[def-complex-exponential]] and
$\chi$ is measured in $\mathrm{J\,s\,C^{-1}}$, so the phase $q\chi/\hbar$ is
dimensionless.

**(v) Field definitions.** The coefficient classes in (ii) are static spatial
data on $\Omega:=\mathbb R^{3}$. For any open time interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$
lift them to $\widetilde{\mathbf A}_{\rm ext}(x,t):=\mathbf A_{\rm ext}(x)$ and
$\widetilde\Phi_{\rm ext}(x,t):=\Phi_{\rm ext}(x)$ on $\Omega\times I$. Define
$$\mathbf B:=\bigl(D_2A_{{\rm ext},3}-D_3A_{{\rm ext},2},\,D_3A_{{\rm ext},1}-D_1A_{{\rm ext},3},\,D_1A_{{\rm ext},2}-D_2A_{{\rm ext},1}\bigr)\in L^\infty(\Omega\times I;\mathbb R^3)\quad\text{in T}.$$
$$\mathbf E:=-\nabla_x\widetilde\Phi_{\rm ext}-\partial_t\widetilde{\mathbf A}_{\rm ext}\in\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I;\mathbb R^3)\quad\text{in }\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}.$$
The curl uses the weak spatial derivatives already required in (ii);
$\partial_t\widetilde{\mathbf A}_{\rm ext}=0$. Here $\mathcal D'$ denotes
vector-valued distributions: each component is a continuous linear functional
on $C_c^\infty(\Omega\times I)$, with continuity meaning that for every compact
$K\subset\Omega\times I$ it is bounded by a constant times the suprema on $K$
of finitely many derivatives of each test function supported in $K$. The
displayed derivatives are distributional derivatives. Explicitly, for every
real test function $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega\times I)$ and component $j$,
$$\langle E_j,\varphi\rangle= \int_{\Omega\times I}\Phi_{\rm ext}(x)\,\partial_{x_j}\varphi(x,t)\,dx\,dt+ \int_{\Omega\times I}A_{{\rm ext},j}(x)\,\partial_t\varphi(x,t)\,dx\,dt.$$
The second integral vanishes for the static lift; the first is well defined
because $\Phi_{\rm ext}\in L^\infty$ and $\varphi$ has compact support. The
same distributional convention applies to the locally integrable
time-dependent coefficients in clause (vi). These are **definitions of the
model's field symbols**; they assert no Maxwell equation, no relation to
measured fields, and no coupling of the particle back on the sources.

**(vi) Gauge transformations.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval.
A real function $\chi:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ is admissible for this
clause when (1) for each $t\in I$, $\chi(\cdot,t)$ is $C^2$ and its first and
second spatial derivatives are bounded uniformly in $t$, and (2) for each
$x\in\Omega$, $t\mapsto\chi(x,t)$ is differentiable on $I$ with
$\partial_t\chi$ bounded on $\Omega\times I$. These bounds make $\chi$ jointly
Lipschitz and continuous; its time derivative is measurable as a pointwise
limit of time difference quotients, and its spatial derivatives are jointly
measurable as limits of spatial difference quotients and agree with their weak
derivatives. For every admissible $\chi$, use the unitary $G_\chi(t)$
defined in [[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]]
clause (c) on $L^2(\Omega;\mathbb C)$. The model relates the pair
$(\mathbf A_{\rm ext},\Phi_{\rm ext})$ to
$$\mathbf A'_{\rm ext}=\mathbf A_{\rm ext}+\nabla\chi,\qquad \Phi'_{\rm ext}=\Phi_{\rm ext}-\partial_{t}\chi,$$
and the state by $\psi'=G_\chi(t)\psi=e^{iq\chi/\hbar}\psi$. The operator consequences,
the criterion under which the multiplier is a symmetry of a fixed model, and
the propagator transported to the transformed pair are proved on this page for
the stated regularity; the **reading** that the two coefficient pairs describe
the same physical situation is part of this assumption, not a theorem, and the
theorem statements of this page are independent of that reading.

**(vii) Status and scope.** Clauses (i)-(vi) are adopted model assumptions for
the declared potential class only. They assert nothing about a laboratory
realization, about field sources, about singular or unbounded potentials,
about time-dependent data beyond the hypotheses of the gauge items, about
statistical or measurement models, or about the accuracy of the spinless
minimal-coupling description of any species; the identification of a physical
arrangement with the model is a tested identification in the sense of P7.
items.physical_scope: The prescribed-external-coupling assumption P5a of the framework: a spinless particle of mass m>0 and charge q in a named Newtonian inertial frame with admissible prescribed potentials (A,Phi) of the bounded-coefficient class, whose energy operator is the minimal-coupling magnetic Schrodinger operator on the domain W^{2,2}; the adopted field definitions, the units, and the adopted gauge transformation of potentials and state phase. Adoption is a model assumption for the stated potential class; it asserts no Maxwell equation or source model, no time-dependent well-posedness beyond the stated class, no derivation from P1-P5, and no identification of any laboratory arrangement or measured field with the declared data.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 3.3 and its subsection 'Gauge transformations', printed pages 45-47 (PDF pages 53-55): the Hamiltonian (3.31) of a charged particle in a magnetic field with minimal coupling, and the gauge transformation of the potentials and of the phase of the wave function (equations (3.43)-(3.45)); PDF page = printed page + 8

J. Zinn-Justin and R. Guida, 'Gauge invariance', Scholarpedia 3(12):8287 (2008), Section 2.2 'Quantum Hamiltonian in a magnetic field and gauge invariance', equations (15)-(18): the unitary transformation U=exp(i e Omega(q)/hbar) transporting the covariant momentum and the Hamiltonian to the gauge-transformed vector potential, and the corresponding transformation of the state phase (their sign convention is A^Omega = A - grad Omega with charge e)

items.title: Conservation of a symmetry generator: commuting flows, energy compatibility and conserved outcome laws
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the
autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] for a declared isolated
system with state space $H$, assigned energy observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$
and flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]); use the symmetry vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]]. Assume the
Axiom of Choice, the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Dependent
Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp observable of the
system with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ and put
$W(s):=e^{-isA/\hbar}$. Then the following are equivalent:

(i) $W(s)U(t)=U(t)W(s)$ for all $s,t\in\mathbb R$;

(ii) $E_A(B)E_H(C)=E_H(C)E_A(B)$ for all Borel sets $B,C\subseteq\mathbb R$;

(iii) $U(t)D(A)=D(A)$ and $U(t)AU(t)^{*}=A$ for all $t\in\mathbb R$.

When they hold:

(a) **Conserved law.** The outcome law of $(A,u_A)$ is time-independent: for
every preparation $\rho$, every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho(0)}(B),\qquad \mu^{A}_{\psi(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\psi(0)}(B)\ \text{for a unit }\psi\ \text{with }\psi(t)=U(t)\psi(0).$$

(b) **Conserved moments.** If $\psi\in D(A)$ is a unit vector, then the mean and
the second moment of the law of $A$ in the pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$ are
finite and independent of $t$, with time-zero values
$\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; if a moment is infinite at
$t=0$, no equality of finite quantities is claimed.

(c) **Unitary symmetries of the dynamics.** If a unitary operator $S$ is a
symmetry in the sense of clause (b) of
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]], that is
$S\,D(H_{\mathrm{op}})=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ and
$S\,H_{\mathrm{op}}=H_{\mathrm{op}}\,S$, then $S\,U(t)=U(t)\,S$ for every $t$;
if in addition $S$ is self-adjoint, then the outcome law of the assigned sharp
observable $(S,u_S)$ with its spectral coordinate unit is time-independent in
every preparation.

(d) **Status and exclusions.** The statement is conditional on P1, P2 and P4
and the cited mathematics. Its symmetry hypothesis is the strong commutation of
the flows or, equivalently, of the spectral measures, not a formal commutator
identity on a small domain; no definite value of a conserved observable is
asserted; no converse from the constancy of laws to the commutation conditions
is claimed for unbounded $A$; and no concrete model potential, apparatus,
measurement record or empirical result is introduced.
items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the state, observable and autonomous-dynamics postulates P1, P2 and P4 for a declared isolated system: for a self-adjoint assigned sharp observable A whose one-parameter unitary group commutes with the flow, the three formulations (commuting flows, strong commutation of the spectral measures, and invariance of the domain of A under the flow with U(t)*AU(t)=A) are equivalent, the outcome law of A is time-independent in every preparation, its mean and second moment are conserved whenever they exist, and a unitary symmetry of the dynamics commutes with the flow, its being self-adjoint making its own outcome law time-independent. The statement asserts no symmetry of any concrete model, no definite value of a conserved observable, no apparatus realization, no equilibration statement and no empirical result, and uses the strong-commutation hypothesis rather than a formal commutator on a small domain.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 4.2, printed pages 115-117 (PDF pages 127-129): commuting self-adjoint operators, Lemma 4.5 and the equivalence with commutation of the one-parameter groups; Theorem 8.1, printed page 174 (PDF page 186): invariant domain and conserved expectations

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Section 3.2, printed pages 20-22 (PDF pages 20-22): the Heisenberg equation, operators commuting with the Hamiltonian and constant Heisenberg representatives

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 4.3-4.4, printed pages 68-71 (PDF pages 76-79): commuting observables, invariance under displacements, conserved quantities and the Heisenberg picture

items.title: Translation invariance of bounded potentials and conservation of momentum
items.statement:
Adopt the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] for a
declared particle of mass parameter $m>0$ and spin label $s$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]), and
assume the Axiom of Choice, the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of
Dependent Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $H_{s}$ be the model's state space with
componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]),
let $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ be real, bounded and measurable, and let
$$H_{V}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2s+1}),\qquad V_{a}(x):=V(x-a),$$
be the model's bounded-potential energy operator with $M_{V}$ multiplication by
$V$ and $T_{a}:=T_{a}^{(2s+1)}$ the componentwise translations
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (c), [[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-translation-covariance]]). Then:

(a) for every $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$:
$$T_{a}H_{V}T_{a}^{-1}=H_{V_{a}},$$
and $T_{a}$ is a symmetry of $H_{V}$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] clause (b)
if and only if $V_{a}=V$ almost everywhere;

(b) if $T_{a}$ is a symmetry for every $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$, then $V$ is almost
everywhere constant; in that case $H_{V}=H_{0}+cI$ on $W^{2,2}$ for
$H_{0}=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}$ and $c$ the constant, and the translations
form a strongly continuous unitary group of symmetries;

(c) **Momentum conservation for translation-invariant models.** Let $V$ be
almost everywhere constant and let $c$ be that constant. Then for every
$k\in\{1,2,3\}$ the momentum component $P_{k}$ is a conserved observable of the
model with energy $H_{V}$: for every preparation $\rho$, every Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{P_{k}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\rho(0)}(B);$$
if $\psi(0)\in D(P_{k})$ is a unit vector, the mean and second moment of the
law of $P_{k}$ are conserved with time-zero values $\langle P_{k}\psi,\psi\rangle$
and $\|P_{k}\psi\|^{2}$; and the coordinate translations satisfy
$T_{te_{k}}=e^{-itP_{k}/\hbar}$ for all $t$, so the generators of the
one-parameter symmetry groups are the momentum components;

(d) **Scope.** The statement concerns the componentwise massive model with real
bounded measurable potentials. It asserts no momentum conservation for a
potential that is not translation invariant — the translation-covariance
theorem transports the position law and conjugates the dynamics, but does not
by itself conserve momentum — and it makes no claim about singular, unbounded,
periodic, boundary or relativistic models, no discrete symmetry group, no
apparatus and no empirical result.
items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the framework postulates for the componentwise massive model with a real bounded measurable potential V: the translation T_a is a symmetry of the bounded-potential operator H_V exactly when V is invariant under translation by a, the full translation group is a symmetry group exactly when V is almost everywhere constant, and for such translation-invariant models the momentum components are conserved observables by the generator-conservation theorem. The statement concerns real bounded measurable potentials only; it asserts no momentum conservation for non-invariant potentials, no statement about singular or unbounded potentials, no lattice or discrete symmetry claim, no apparatus realization and no empirical result.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 4.1.1, 4.2 and 4.3, printed pages 59-69 (PDF pages 67-77): translating kets, the momentum as generator of translations, and translational invariance with conservation of momentum

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 8.1, printed pages 173-175 (PDF pages 185-187): the one-parameter unitary group of translations, its generator, and momentum conservation for the free motion; Theorem 8.1 printed page 174 (PDF page 186)
B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Section 3.2, printed pages 20-22 (PDF pages 20-22): conserved operators as those commuting with the Hamiltonian

items.title: Rotational and parity invariance of bounded-potential models: symmetries and conservation of angular momentum and parity laws
items.statement:
Adopt the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] for a
declared particle of mass parameter $m>0$ and spin label $s$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom of
Choice, the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Dependent Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$r=2s+1$, be the model's state space with componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$,
let $U(R)$ be the spatial rotation action and $\Pi$ the spatial parity action
([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]],
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-parity-action]]), let $U_{i}(t)=U(R_{i}(t))$ be the
coordinate rotation subgroups with Stone generators $L_{i}$ on the Schwartz
classes ([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]]), let
$V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ be real, bounded and measurable, and let
$$H_{V}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),\qquad V_{R}(x):=V(R^{-1}x),\quad V_{P}(x):=V(-x),$$
be the model's bounded-potential energy operator with flow
$U(t)=\exp(-itH_{V}/\hbar)$ in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (b)
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (c) applied componentwise,
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a)).
Then:

(a) for every $R\in SO(3)$ one has $U(R)H_{V}U(R)^{-1}=H_{V_{R}}$, and $U(R)$
is a symmetry of $H_{V}$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] clause (b)
if and only if $V_{R}=V$ almost everywhere;

(b) if $V_{R}=V$ almost everywhere for every $R\in SO(3)$, then every $U(R)$
is a symmetry, the map $R\mapsto U(R)$ is a strongly continuous unitary
symmetry group of the declared dynamics, and each generator $L_{i}$ is a
conserved observable of the model with energy $H_{V}$ in the unit
$\mathrm{J\,s}$ of the model's action
([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]): for every preparation $\rho$,
every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{L_{i}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{L_{i}}_{\rho(0)}(B),$$
and for a unit vector $\psi(0)\in D(L_{i})$ the mean and second moment of the
law of $L_{i}$ are finite and independent of $t$, with time-zero values
$\langle L_{i}\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|L_{i}\psi\|^{2}$;

(c) if $V(-x)=V(x)$ for almost every $x$, then $\Pi H_{V}\Pi=H_{V}$ on
$W^{2,2}$, so $\Pi$ is a symmetry of $H_{V}$, and $\Pi$ is a symmetry if and
only if $V_{P}=V$ almost everywhere; moreover, reading the self-adjoint
unitary $\Pi$ as an assigned sharp observable with its spectral coordinate in
the dimensionless unit of its eigenvalues $\pm1$, the outcome law of $\Pi$ is
time-independent in every preparation:
$$\mu^{\Pi}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{\Pi}_{\rho(0)}(B)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel},\ t\in\mathbb R);$$

(d) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the
cited mathematics, and it concerns the componentwise massive model with real
bounded measurable potentials. Rotations and parity act on the spatial factor
only: no SU(2) lift, no rotation of the internal factor and no spin angular
momentum are introduced. The rotational and parity invariance hypotheses are
exactly the displayed almost-everywhere identities; no concrete potential,
apparatus, measured spectrum or empirical result is asserted, and no
characterization of the invariant potentials beyond these identities is
claimed.
items.physical_scope: Conditional symmetry and conservation statements for the massive spin-s model with a real bounded measurable potential: spatial rotations conjugate the bounded-potential energy operator to the rotated potential, rotational invariance makes every rotation a symmetry and the coordinate-rotation generators conserved sharp observables, and parity invariance makes the parity action a symmetry with a time-independent parity outcome law. The item asserts no symmetry of any concrete potential outside the stated invariance hypotheses, no spinorial or internal rotation action, no SU(2) lift, no apparatus and no empirical result.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 4.1.3-4.3, printed pages 62-70 (PDF pages 70-78): the rotation operator and its generators, parity and vector operators, symmetry of the Hamiltonian and conservation laws; PDF page = printed page + 8

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Section 3.2, printed pages 20-22 (PDF pages 20-22): conserved operators as those commuting with the Hamiltonian and their constant Heisenberg representatives

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 9 'Angular Momentum', Sections 1.2-1.3, printed pages 6-11 (PDF pages 6-11): the angular momentum operators and their commutation relations, and the commutativity of the angular momentum operators with any central-potential Hamiltonian (equation (1.70))

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 8.1, printed pages 173-175 (PDF pages 185-187) and Theorem 8.1 printed page 174 (PDF page 186): conserved quantities and commuting self-adjoint operators

items.title: Gauge covariance of the prescribed-coupling model: unitary equivalence, the symmetry criterion and the transported propagator
items.statement:
Adopt the postulates P1, P2 and P4 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] clause (a),
for a **declared isolated system** whose energy operator is the
prescribed-coupling minimal-coupling operator of
[[post-nrqm-symmetries-prescribed-external-coupling]]: a declared spinless
particle of mass parameter $m>0$ and charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$, with
admissible prescribed potentials $(\mathbf A_{\rm ext},\Phi_{\rm ext})$ and
energy operator $K_{\mathbf A_{\rm ext},\Phi_{\rm ext}}$ on the domain
$W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
([[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-magnetic-schrodinger-operator]]).
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$
be an open interval and let $\chi:\mathbb R^{3}\times I\to\mathbb R$ be a real
gauge function satisfying the two regularity hypotheses of
[[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-gauge-h2-domain-preservation]]
(for every $t$, $\chi(\cdot,t)$ is $C^{2}$ with bounded first and second
spatial derivatives, uniformly in $t$; and $t\mapsto\chi(x,t)$ is
differentiable with bounded $\partial_{t}\chi$). Put
$$\theta(x,t):=\frac{q}{\hbar}\chi(x,t),\qquad A'_{j}(\cdot,t):=A_{j}+D_{j}\chi(\cdot,t),\qquad \Phi'(\cdot,t):=\Phi_{\rm ext}-\partial_{t}\chi(\cdot,t),$$
let $G(t)$ be multiplication by $e^{i\theta(\cdot,t)}$, and put
$K:=K_{\mathbf A_{\rm ext},\Phi_{\rm ext}}$,
$H'(t):=K_{\mathbf A'(t),\Phi'(t)}$ and $U(\tau):=e^{-i\tau K/\hbar}$. Then:

(a) **Gauge conjugation and unitary equivalence.** If $\chi$ does not depend
on $t$, then $G:=G(t)$ is independent of $t$, is unitary with
$G\,W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, and
$$G\,K\,G^{-1}=K_{\mathbf A_{\rm ext}+\nabla\chi,\Phi_{\rm ext}},\qquad e^{-itK_{\mathbf A_{\rm ext}+\nabla\chi,\Phi_{\rm ext}}/\hbar}=G\,e^{-itK/\hbar}\,G^{-1}\quad(t\in\mathbb R):$$
the two prescribed-coupling models are related by the fixed unitary $G$.

(b) **Symmetry criterion and the global-phase case.** For every $t\in I$ the
operator $G(t)$ is unitary, preserves $W^{2,2}$, and is a symmetry of the
declared dynamics with energy $K$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] clause (b)
**if and only if**
$$K_{\mathbf A'(t),\Phi_{\rm ext}}=K_{\mathbf A_{\rm ext},\Phi_{\rm ext}},$$
that is, if and only if transporting the vector potential while keeping the
original scalar potential reproduces the original operator. In particular, if
$\chi$ is constant, then $\mathbf A'(t)=\mathbf A_{\rm ext}$,
$\Phi'(t)=\Phi_{\rm ext}$ and $G(t)=e^{i\theta}I$ for the constant
$\theta=q\chi/\hbar$, so that every $G(t)$ is a symmetry of the declared
dynamics (a global phase). No claim is made in the nonconstant case beyond the
displayed criterion.

(c) **Transported propagator and the time-dependent model.** For the general
gauge function of the statement and every $u_{0}\in W^{2,2}$ and $s\in I$, the
curve
$$u(t):=G(t)\,U(t-s)\,G(s)^{-1}u_{0}\qquad(t\in I)$$
lies in $W^{2,2}$, is differentiable into $L^{2}$ on $I$, satisfies
$u(s)=u_{0}$ and $i\hbar\,u'(t)=H'(t)u(t)$ for every $t$, and is the unique
such curve; the two-parameter family $U'(t,s):=G(t)U(t-s)G(s)^{-1}$ consists of
unitaries mapping $W^{2,2}$ onto $W^{2,2}$, with $U'(t,t)=I$ and
$U'(t,r)U'(r,s)=U'(t,s)$. Moreover
$$H'(t)=G(t)\,K\,G(t)^{-1}-q\,\partial_{t}\chi(\cdot,t),$$
so the family $G(t)$ relates the autonomous model with energy $K$ to the
transformed model whose generator is $G(t)KG(t)^{-1}-q\partial_{t}\chi$; a
genuinely time-dependent family $G(t)$ is a family of unitaries indexed by
time and is not claimed to be a symmetry of the autonomous dynamics except at
those $t$ where the operator identity of (b) holds.

(d) **Scope.** The statement concerns the prescribed spinless
minimal-coupling model with admissible bounded-coefficient potentials and the
stated gauge regularity, and is conditional on P1, P2, P4 and P5a and the
cited operator analysis. It asserts no Maxwell equation, no source or
back-reaction model, no identification of the two coefficient pairs as
descriptions of one physical situation (that reading is part of P5a), no
statement about singular or unbounded potentials, and no apparatus or
empirical result; the gauge multipliers are unitary transformations between
coefficient classes and are symmetries of the fixed dynamics exactly under the
criterion displayed in (b).

items.title: Scope and empirical status of the symmetry and conservation items
items.statement:
## What the page establishes

The items of this page are conditional consequences of the framework's
postulates and of the cited mathematics.
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] fixes the
vocabulary: a symmetry of the declared dynamics is a unitary preserving the
energy domain and commuting with the energy operator, a unitary symmetry group
is a group of such symmetries, a conserved sharp observable is one whose
outcome law is time-independent in every preparation, and the translations,
spatial rotations, parity and gauge multipliers are recorded as the model's
candidate actions, not as symmetries.
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-unitary-conjugation-and-commutation-calculus]] proves the
equivalence between flow commutation, strong spectral commutation and domain
invariance of a self-adjoint observable;
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]],
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-parity-action]],
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]] and
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-free-flow-multiplier-form]] provide the concrete actions
and their operator identities on the component-valued model.
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-generator-conservation]] proves the equivalence of the
commutation conditions with the conservation of the outcome law and the
conservation of moments, and covers self-adjoint unitary symmetries;
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-translation-invariance-and-momentum-conservation]]
decides exactly which bounded potentials have the translations as symmetries
and derives momentum conservation for the translation-invariant case;
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-rotational-and-parity-invariance]] does the same for
rotations (with conservation of the coordinate-rotation generators) and for
parity; and [[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-gauge-covariance]] transports the
prescribed-coupling operator under gauge transformations of
[[post-nrqm-symmetries-prescribed-external-coupling]], exhibits the exact
criterion under which a gauge multiplier is a symmetry of the fixed dynamics
and identifies the global-phase case. Every one of these statements is
conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, P5a and P6 in their stated readings, on the
choice assumptions displayed with the items, and on the cited operator
analysis.

## Empirical status of the symmetry and conservation statements

The conservation laws proved here are model consequences: they hold for the
declared massive model with the displayed potential class and follow from the
invariance hypotheses as identities about that model. They are not reports of
measurements and do not establish that any laboratory preparation is exactly
described by the model. In particular, the mass parameter $m>0$, the charge
parameter $q$, the spin label $s$ and the potentials $(\mathbf A_{\rm ext},\Phi_{\rm ext})$
are declared model data in the units of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the statement that a concrete
species, field configuration or apparatus realizes them is a tested
identification with uncertainty, external to these items. A selection rule or
a conservation law deduced here becomes an empirical prediction only after a
preparation map, a detection model, a sampling model and an uncertainty
budget are supplied, none of which this page provides. The agreement of such
an identified model with data is evidence about the combined model and
apparatus assumptions; it is not a proof of the postulates.

## What is not claimed

The page asserts no symmetry of any concrete potential outside the displayed
almost-everywhere invariance hypotheses, no classification of centrally
symmetric or parity-even systems beyond those hypotheses, no definite value
of a conserved observable, and no converse from the constancy of outcome laws
to the commutation conditions for unbounded observables. The rotation and
parity actions act on the spatial factor only: no SU(2) lift, no rotation of
the internal factor and no spin angular momentum appear here; antiunitary and
time-reversal symmetries, superselection sectors, gauge freedom beyond the
prescribed bounded-coefficient class, singular or unbounded potentials,
confined and boundary realizations, periodic potentials, time-dependent
external fields, relativistic matter and full field theory are all outside
the scope of these items and require their own model assumptions.

`thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-gauge-h2-domain-preservation` and
`thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-gauge-transported-propagator`); the
mathematical content of those items is proved locally by their own complete
arguments, which is what this page consumes, and the citation repair belongs to
their owning batch.

items.title: Definite parity of nondegenerate eigenstates and the position-matrix-element selection rule
items.statement:
Adopt the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] for a
declared particle of mass parameter $m>0$ and spin label $s$, with state space
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, $r=2s+1$, componentwise operators
$Q_{j},P_{k}$ and the parity action $\Pi$
([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-parity-action]]); assume the Axiom of Countable Choice
and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ be real, bounded
and measurable with
$$V(-x)=V(x)\qquad\text{for almost every }x\in\mathbb R^{3},$$
let
$$H_{V}=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),$$
and put $V_{P}(x):=V(-x)$. Then:

(a) if $\psi\in D(H_{V})$ is an eigenvector of $H_{V}$ with eigenvalue
$E\in\mathbb R$, $H_{V}\psi=E\psi$ and $\psi\ne0$, then $\Pi\psi$ is again an
eigenvector of $H_{V}$ with the same eigenvalue $E$; consequently every
eigenspace of $H_{V}$ is invariant under $\Pi$;

(b) if the eigenspace of $E$ is one-dimensional, then $\Pi\psi=\lambda\psi$
with $\lambda\in\{-1,1\}$: the state has definite parity;

(c) if $\psi,\psi'\in H_{s}$ are unit vectors with $\Pi\psi=\sigma\psi$ and
$\Pi\psi'=\tau\psi'$ for signs $\sigma,\tau\in\{-1,1\}$ and $\psi\in D(Q_{j})$,
then
$$\sigma=\tau\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\langle Q_{j}\psi,\psi'\rangle=0;$$
the position matrix element of two states of equal parity vanishes, while no
nonvanishing statement is made for opposite parities;

(d) **Scope.** The example is conditional on the postulates and the cited
mathematics; the matrix element of (c) is an identity about the model's
assigned position observables. No transition rate, no spectral intensity, no
time-dependent coupling, no measurement model and no empirical consequence is
computed; the hypothesis that the relevant eigenvalue is nondegenerate is
essential for (b).
items.physical_scope: A model computation for the massive spin-s model with an even real bounded measurable potential: the parity invariance of every energy eigenspace, the definite parity of nondegenerate eigenstates, and the vanishing of the position matrix element between two states of the same parity. The item is a conditional identity about the model's operators and assigned position observables; it computes no transition rate, models no measurement and records no empirical result.

items.title: The free model: translation symmetries and conserved momentum in the momentum representation
items.statement:
Adopt the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] for a
declared particle of mass parameter $m>0$ and spin label $s$, with state space
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, $r=2s+1$, componentwise operators
$Q_{j},P_{k}$ and translations $T_{a}$
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (c));
assume the Axiom of Choice, the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of
Dependent Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]). Consider the **free model**, the bounded-potential
model with $V\equiv0$:
$$H_{0}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2},\qquad D(H_{0})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),$$
with flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{0}/\hbar)$, momentum unitary $U^{(r)}$
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]]) and
$f_{t}(p):=e^{-it|p|^{2}/(2m\hbar)}$. Then:

(a) for every $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$ the translation $T_{a}$ is a symmetry of
$H_{0}$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] clause (b),
and
$$T_{a}\,e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\,T_{a}^{-1}=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\qquad(a\in\mathbb R^{3},\ t\in\mathbb R);$$

(b) in the momentum representation the two actions are the multipliers
$$U^{(r)}T_{a}U^{(r)-1}=M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}},\qquad U^{(r)}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}U^{(r)-1}=M_{f_{t}},$$
which commute; consequently $T_{a}U(t)=U(t)T_{a}$ for all $a,t$;

(c) **Momentum conservation.** For every $k$ the momentum component $P_{k}$ is
a conserved observable of the free model: for every preparation $\rho$, Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and $t$,
$$\mu^{P_{k}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\rho(0)}(B),$$
and for a unit vector $\psi(0)\in D(P_{k})$ the mean and second moment of the
law of $P_{k}$ are finite and independent of $t$, with time-zero values
$\langle P_{k}\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|P_{k}\psi\|^{2}$; the coordinate
translations satisfy $T_{te_{k}}=e^{-itP_{k}/\hbar}$, so the momentum
components are the generators of the translational symmetry groups;

(d) the modulus of the momentum representative is invariant in time:
$$\bigl|\bigl(U^{(r)}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\psi\bigr)(p)\bigr|=\bigl|\bigl(U^{(r)}\psi\bigr)(p)\bigr|\qquad\text{for almost every }p\ \text{and every }\psi\in H_{s};$$
consequently the squared modulus of the momentum representative is the same
almost-everywhere function of $p$ at every time;

(e) **Scope.** The statement concerns the free model $V\equiv0$ only. For a
nonconstant bounded potential the translations need not be symmetries and
momentum need not be conserved; that failure is exhibited on this page. No
trajectory in space, no classical limit, no measurement model and no empirical
result is asserted.
items.physical_scope: A model computation for the free massive spin-s model, V identically zero: the translations are symmetries and commute with the free flow, the momentum components are conserved sharp observables with conserved law and moments, and the free flow acts in the momentum representation as a unimodular multiplier leaving the modulus of the momentum representative fixed. The item asserts nothing for nonconstant potentials, no trajectory, no measured distribution, and no apparatus model.

items.title: A bounded nonconstant potential with no nontrivial translational symmetry
items.statement:
Let $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ be any real, bounded, measurable, nonconstant
function. Then for every nonzero $a\in\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\}$ the
translation $T_{a}$ is a symmetry of the declared bounded-potential dynamics
with energy $H_{V}$.
items.physical_scope: A counterexample inside the declared massive model with a bounded measurable potential: the indicator of the unit ball has no nontrivial translational symmetry, so no nonzero translation commutes with its bounded-potential energy operator, while the potential itself is bounded and measurable and its model is self-adjoint on W^{2,2}. The item refutes a universal claim about translations of bounded nonconstant potentials; it asserts nothing about the physics of a laboratory potential and records no measurement.

items.title: A radial bounded potential: rotational and parity symmetry and conservation of the rotation generators
items.statement:
Adopt the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] for a
declared particle of mass parameter $m>0$ and spin label $s$, with state space
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, $r=2s+1$, componentwise operators
$Q_{j},P_{k}$, rotation action $U(R)$ and coordinate-rotation generators
$L_{i}$ ([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]],
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]]); assume the
Axiom of Choice, the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Dependent
Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $v:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be bounded and
measurable, and let $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ be real, bounded and
measurable with
$$V(x)=v(|x|)\qquad\text{for almost every }x\in\mathbb R^{3},$$
a **radial potential almost everywhere** (if $V$ is the composition
$x\mapsto v(|x|)$ everywhere, this holds with empty exceptional set). Let
$$H_{V}=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),$$
be the bounded-potential energy operator. Then:

(a) for every $R\in SO(3)$ one has $V(R^{-1}x)=V(x)$ for almost every $x$, and
$V(-x)=V(x)$ for almost every $x$;

(b) every $U(R)$ is a symmetry of $H_{V}$, the map $R\mapsto U(R)$ is a
strongly continuous unitary symmetry group of the declared dynamics, and each
generator $L_{i}$ is a conserved observable: for every preparation $\rho$,
Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and $t$,
$$\mu^{L_{i}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{L_{i}}_{\rho(0)}(B),$$
with conserved mean and second moment for unit vectors in $D(L_{i})$ and
time-zero values $\langle L_{i}\psi,\psi\rangle$, $\|L_{i}\psi\|^{2}$, in the
unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$ of the model's action
([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]);

(c) the parity action $\Pi$ is a symmetry of $H_{V}$, and its outcome law in
every preparation is time-independent;

(d) **Scope.** The example is conditional on the postulates and the bounded
radial class; it computes no eigenvalue, no bound state, no degeneracy and no
radial solution, and the boundedness of $v$ excludes the Coulomb potential and
other unbounded radial models, which require their own self-adjointness and
spectral analysis. No claim is made that any particular physical potential is
radial, and no empirical result is recorded.
items.physical_scope: A model example for the massive spin-s model with a bounded measurable potential that is radial almost everywhere: every spatial rotation is a symmetry, the rotation action is a strongly continuous unitary symmetry group, the coordinate-rotation generators are conserved sharp observables in J s, and the parity action is a symmetry with a conserved parity law. The item is conditional on the bounded radial class; it asserts no eigenvalue, bound-state or degeneracy claim, no Coulomb or other unbounded radial model, and no empirical result.

items.title: What the worked items of the symmetry companion page establish
items.statement:
## The worked items and what they establish

[[ex-nrqm-symmetries-free-translation-and-momentum]] is the exact free-model
computation: with $V\equiv0$ every translation is a symmetry, the free flow in
the momentum representation is the unimodular multiplier
$M_{f_{t}}$, $f_{t}(p)=e^{-it|p|^{2}/(2m\hbar)}$, the translations are the
multipliers $M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}}$, and the momentum components are
conserved sharp observables with the law, moment and generator statements of
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-translation-invariance-and-momentum-conservation]];
the modulus of the momentum representative is invariant in time almost
everywhere.
[[cex-nrqm-symmetries-nonconstant-potential-breaks-translation]] shows that
this fails as soon as the potential is nonconstant in the relevant direction:
for the bounded measurable indicator potential $1_{B(0,1)}$ no nonzero
translation is a symmetry, because the shifted potential differs from the
original on a set of positive measure, so the symmetry criterion of the
translation theorem is not met.
[[ex-nrqm-symmetries-parity-selection-rule]] derives, for a potential even
almost everywhere, that every energy eigenspace is invariant under the parity
action, that a nondegenerate eigenstate has definite parity, and that the
position matrix element of two states of equal parity vanishes.
[[ex-nrqm-symmetries-central-potential-rotation-invariance]] verifies the
almost-everywhere rotational and parity invariance of a bounded radial
potential and instantiates
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-rotational-and-parity-invariance]]: all rotations are
symmetries, the rotation action is a strongly continuous unitary symmetry
group, and the coordinate-rotation generators $L_{i}$ are conserved sharp
observables, with the underlying conservation mechanism of
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-generator-conservation]].

## What none of the items establishes

None of the four items is an experiment: no apparatus, preparation map,
calibration, detection model, efficiency, resolution, background model,
sampling model, uncertainty budget, count or dataset appears, and no measured
value of any model parameter is asserted. The objects $m$, $q$ when present,
$s$, the potentials and the conserved laws are model data and model statements
in the units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; deciding that a
laboratory system realizes the model, that its potential is approximately
radial or even, or that a transition amplitude is the matrix element computed
here, is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and
apparatus assumptions, and it is external to this page. In particular the
parity selection rule is an identity about the model's assigned position
observables: turning it into a statement about observed intensities requires a
time-dependent coupling model, the corresponding transition-rate analysis, a
detection model and a sampling model, none of which is supplied here.

## Limits of the statements

The free computation is conditional on $V\equiv0$; the counterexample concerns
one potential inside the bounded measurable class and refutes only the
universal claim that every bounded nonconstant potential has all nonzero
translations as symmetries (potentials constant along a direction keep the
corresponding translations). The central-potential example assumes the radial
identity almost everywhere and a bounded radial function; it asserts no
eigenvalue, bound state, degeneracy, radial solution or spectral line, and its
boundedness hypothesis excludes the Coulomb and other unbounded radial
models. The parity example requires the evenness hypothesis and, for definite
parity, the nondegeneracy of the eigenvalue; at a degenerate eigenvalue only
the eigenspace invariance is asserted. No item of this page makes a claim about
antiunitary or time-reversal symmetries, about superselection, about spinorial
rotations or the internal factor, or about relativistic and field-theoretic
structures.
